---
title: Warehouse safety
department: operations
status: current
---
Warehouse safety at Northwind is enforced through three mechanisms: mandatory
personal protective equipment, segregation of powered equipment from people, and
an incident reporting culture that does not punish the reporter.

High visibility vests are required anywhere on the operations floor, including
the mezzanine and the yard. Steel toe footwear is required in the inbound dock,
the outbound dock and the pallet aisles, but not in the pick module or the
packing benches where no powered equipment operates.

Forklifts and reach trucks operate only inside marked lanes. Where a lane
crosses a pedestrian route the crossing is controlled by a mirror and a floor
marking, and the pedestrian has priority. A driver who proceeds through a
crossing without stopping is subject to immediate removal from the equipment
register.

Any contact between powered equipment and a person is a category one incident
regardless of injury. The depot duty manager pages the regional safety team
within five minutes and the escalation window does not pause out of hours. Near
misses are reported through the same channel with a lower severity, and the
operations team reviews near miss volume as a leading indicator.

Manual handling limits are twenty three kilograms for a lift from floor to waist
and sixteen kilograms above shoulder height. Loads above these limits require a
second person or a lifting aid. A parcel exceeding twenty three kilograms should
have been flagged at induction and its presence in the pick module is itself a
reportable finding.

Blocked fire exits are the most frequent audit failure across the network. A tote
stack, a roll cage or a pallet placed within one metre of an exit route must be
cleared immediately by whoever notices it, without waiting for a supervisor.

Depot safety performance is reviewed monthly alongside dock arrival times and
incident volume. A depot with rising near miss counts and falling incident counts
is treated as under reporting, not as improving.
